Batch audit: 25 runs. 15 were accepted, 9 declined (r01, r03, r04, r06, r09, r10, r16, r20, r24) and 1 was not reported (r23).
Flagged 7 of the 15 accepted runs:
- r02, r05, r11, r12, r25 (summary outlier): the centre strain-rate (REGR) peak is about 84 %/h (z ≈ 104), roughly twice the batch median of 42.4 %/h. Peak position (316 µm) and growth-zone length match the batch. Each run kept 2 remedies. I only opened r02's full record: its 2 remedies cut the frame stride from 6 to 3 to 1. I did not open the full records of the other four, so I haven't confirmed that their remedies were stride cuts.
- r17, r18 (width-free ratio used): both are reported with the width-free ratio, so the plane-sections check was not run. Their largest ratio is far from the other width-free runs (z = -3.64 and +3.24), and no check that was run covers the flank kinematics.
Cleared 8: r07, r08, r13, r14, r15, r19, r21, r22. Every check that was run passed and every summary is within |z| ≤ 1.2.
What the flagged runs have in common: all 7 pass every check that was run. The problems only show when the summaries are compared with the batch. For r02, the most likely cause is that cutting the frame stride doubled the strain rate without moving the peak position or changing the zone length, which the checks don't detect. For r17 and r18, the width-free path left the flank curvature-rate kinematics without a check.
